speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned sudden-onset vertigo; can you describe exactly how you feel when this spinning sensation starts, and do you experience any nausea, hearing changes, or dizziness when you move your head?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV).

The clinical picture of sudden, brief (3-minute) spinning vertigo triggered by movement (going to bed) without other neurological deficits is classic for BPPV. Since the patient feels back to baseline and has no hearing loss, no further imaging or labs are required; a Dix-Hallpike maneuver can be performed to confirm the diagnosis.
